original_question: What non-perturbative microscopic framework can describe large-amplitude collective motion in odd-A nuclei, or more generally in systems with several quasiparticles present, while treating the interplay between single-particle motion and collective motion in a unified way rather than starting from a small-amplitude particle-vibration-coupling approximation?
target_in_paper: Non-perturbative method capable of treating LACM in odd-A nuclei (generally speaking, LACM in the presence of several quasiparticles) is lacking, however.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the need for a non-perturbative microscopic framework, focuses on large-amplitude collective motion (LACM) in odd-A nuclei and systems with multiple quasiparticles, and highlights the requirement to unify single-particle and collective modes rather than relying on small-amplitude particle–vibration coupling approximations.
missing_details: Explicit definition of LACM as tunneling between different HFB local minima at zero temperature
Reference to the Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (HFB) mean‐field and quasiparticle vacuum framework
Mention of the perturbative RPA/QRPA‐based particle–vibration‐coupling methods currently in use
Specification of the desired extension of the adiabatic self‐consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) or time‐dependent HFB (TDHFB) approach
Clarification that the question is posed in the context of cold (zero‐temperature) nuclei
Emphasis on constructing the collective submanifold and deriving a collective Hamiltonian non‐perturbatively
refined_question:
In the framework of zero‐temperature nuclear large‐amplitude collective motion, what fully microscopic, non‐perturbative extension of the adiabatic self‐consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) method—or an alternative approach based on time‐dependent Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (TDHFB) theory—can be developed to treat odd‐A nuclei (i.e.
systems with one or more quasiparticles on an HFB vacuum) so as to self‐consistently construct the collective submanifold and derive a collective Hamiltonian that describes tunneling between distinct HFB local minima, while simultaneously accounting for the coupling and interplay between quasiparticle degrees of freedom and collective coordinates beyond the perturbative RPA/QRPA‐based particle–vibration‐coupling approximations?
justification: The refined question incorporates all domain‐specific definitions and scope: it specifies cold (zero‐temperature) nuclei, the HFB/quasiparticle framework, the ASCC and TDHFB methods, and the goal of constructing the collective submanifold and Hamiltonian non‐perturbatively. It remains tightly bound to the paper’s open problem as stated in section 6.8, without broadening to adjacent problems or speculative extensions.
